<!-- mv-section: id={{id}} type=ai-scoring -->
## Machine scores and human scores

<!-- The -data chunk makes these objects for the text and the questions; the -prep chunk
     makes them again for the exercises, which learnr runs in a fresh environment. -->

```{r {{id}}-data, include = FALSE}
scores <- lab$scores
.tk_audit <- mirtverse::ai_audit(scores{{audit_args}})
```

```{r {{id}}-prep, include = FALSE}
scores <- lab$scores
```

### Do the machine and the raters agree?

`scores` holds `r nrow(scores)` written responses that an automated engine
scored. People also scored `r sum(!is.na(scores$human1))` of them, the
validity sample. Before the engine's scores count, they must agree with the
people's scores as well as two people agree with each other, overall and
within each group of students.

`agreement_report()` gives the quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) between the
machine and the first rater, the standardized mean difference (SMD) between
their scores, and a verdict against the rules in `mv_rules()`. Save it as
`agree`.

```{r {{id}}-agree, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "{{id}}-prep"}
agree <- agreement_report(scores$machine, scores$human1{{agree_args}})
agree
```

```{r {{id}}-agree-check}
lab_need(exists("agree") && inherits(agree, "mv_agreement"),
         "Save the result of agreement_report() as `agree`.")
.n <- sum(agree$verdict != "meets", na.rm = TRUE)
if (.n) sprintf("%d row(s) do not meet the rules. Read the verdict column to see which.", .n) else
  "Every row meets the rules."
```

```{r {{id}}-q-smd}
question_radio(
  "The machine's QWK with the raters is high, but its SMD for one group is -0.30. What does that mean?",
  answer("The machine ranks responses much as the raters do, but gives that group's responses lower scores than the raters do.",
         correct = TRUE,
         message = "Right. QWK measures agreement in order; SMD measures a shift in level. A fair engine needs both."),
  answer("The engine is accurate, so the difference must be in the students.",
         message = "The SMD compares machine and human scores of the same responses, so it is about the engine, not the students."),
  answer("Nothing: SMD only matters when QWK is low.",
         message = "A high QWK can hide a constant shift for one group; that is why the rules check SMD within groups."),
  allow_retry = TRUE, random_answer_order = TRUE)
```

### A full audit

`ai_audit()` runs all the checks at once: Agreement, bias overall and
within groups, differential scoring (machine minus human for students with
the same human score) and, when there are several periods, drift. Each
problem becomes a flag: `block` means the scores should not be used as they
are, `review` means a person must look first.

```{r {{id}}-audit, exercise = TRUE, exercise.setup = "{{id}}-prep"}
audit <- ai_audit(scores{{audit_args}})
audit
```

```{r {{id}}-audit-check}
lab_need(exists("audit") && inherits(audit, "mv_audit"),
         "Save the result of ai_audit() as `audit`.")
sprintf("%d flag(s): %d block, %d review. autoplot(audit) shows where they are.",
        nrow(audit$flags), sum(audit$flags$level == "block"), sum(audit$flags$level == "review"))
```

```{r {{id}}-q-decision}
.tk_st <- .tk_audit$checks$status
.tk_dec <- if (any(.tk_st == "block")) 1L else if (any(.tk_st == "review")) 2L else 3L
.tk_why <- c("At least one check blocks: Fix the engine or route the affected responses to people first.",
             "Nothing blocks, but some checks need a person's review before the scores count.",
             "No check is flagged; keep monitoring agreement and fairness in every administration.")[.tk_dec]
question_radio(
  "Based on the audit, can the engine score these responses on its own?",
  answer("No: Not until the blocking problems are fixed.", correct = .tk_dec == 1L, message = .tk_why),
  answer("Only with human review of the flagged parts.", correct = .tk_dec == 2L, message = .tk_why),
  answer("Yes, with ongoing monitoring.", correct = .tk_dec == 3L, message = .tk_why),
  allow_retry = TRUE)
```

`validity_argument(audit, construct = "...", use = "...")` turns the audit
into the start of a validity argument for the people who decide how the
scores are used.
